slides.title: Slide 7
slides.text:
Scaling Up: The Ecologist’s Calculation Algorithm
The Scenario: You throw 10 quadrats (each measuring 1m?) randomly in a field that has a total area of 1000m2.
You count a total of 30 dandelions across all 10 quadrats. How many dandelions are in the whole field?
Step 1: Calculate the MEAN number of organisms per quadrat.
Formula: Total organisms counted + Number of quadrats used
Calculation: 30 + 10 = 3 | dandelions per quadrat (Mean)
Step 2: Calculate the area of ONE quadrat.
Calculation: 1m x 1m= 1m? |
Step 3: Calculate how many quadrats fit in the total habitat.
Formula: Total Area + Quadrat Area
Calculation: 1000m? + 1m? = | 1000 | quadrats
Step 4: Scale up to estimate the total population.
Formula: Mean per quadrat x Total possible quadrats
Calculation: 3 x 1000 = FeReleleye Eire (felt in the field.
(Footnote: If assessing data spread in exams, remember: Mode = most common number, Median = middle number when lined up in size Order). em cemini notebook
